question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + z &=4 \\ 2 y + z &=-1 \\ - x + 2 y + z &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & - \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & - \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3 \\ y &=-1 \\ z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

So, we have the solution $x=3$, $y=-1$, and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle 3,-1,1\rangle$.
